1.title: Microsoft Entra Users, Groups and Licenses
1.text: Welcome to Module one: Microsoft Entra Users, Groups and Licenses. It covers the exam area Manage Azure identities and governance. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Create users and groups. Manage user and group properties. Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra I D. Manage external users. Configure self-service password reset (S S P R). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Manage Azure identities and governance (twenty-twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: Users and groups
1.text: Users and groups. Microsoft Entra I D is Microsoft's cloud identity service. A tenant is a dedicated instance of it for an organization. Member user. A work account in your tenant. Guest user. An external person invited into your tenant (B to B collaboration). Group, type Security. Used to manage access to resources and apps. Group, type Microsoft three sixty-five. A collaboration group (shared mailbox, calendar, Teams). Assigned membership. You add members. Dynamic membership. Rules add and remove members automatically (needs Microsoft Entra I D P one or higher).

1.title: Users and groups, continued
1.text: Users and groups. The figure shows this: Users and groups in a Microsoft Entra tenant, with assigned and dynamic membership.

1.title: Users and groups, continued
1.text: Users and groups. You can create users one at a time, in bulk with a C S V file in the portal, or with Power Shell or the C L I. Deleted users stay recoverable for thirty days. User and group properties (job title, department, usage location, manager) can be edited, and dynamic groups use properties such as department in their rules. Exam tip: "Add users to a group automatically based on department" equals a dynamic group. It requires P one or higher.

1.title: Licenses
1.text: Licenses. Licenses (for example Microsoft three sixty-five or Entra I D P one or P two) are assigned to users or groups. Usage location. A user must have a usage location before a license can be assigned. Group-based licensing. Assign a license to a group; all members get it; new members get it automatically. Errors. Not enough licenses or conflicting service plans show as license assignment errors. Exam tip: "License assignment fails for a user" equals check the usage location and the available licenses.

1.title: External users
1.text: External users. Invite. Invite a guest by email; they accept the invitation. Guest access. Guests get limited default permissions; control them with external collaboration settings. Use. Give guests access with groups and R B A C roles, like members.

1.title: Self-service password reset (SSPR)
1.text: Self-service password reset (S S P R). S S P R lets users reset their own passwords without calling the help desk. Scope. Enable for all users, a selected group, or none. Authentication methods. The user proves identity with the number of methods required (one or two): phone, email, authenticator app, security questions. Registration. Users register their methods; can be required at sign-in. Password writeback. Sends the new password back to on-premises Active Directory in a hybrid setup (needs a paid license and Entra Connect).

1.title: Self-service password reset (SSPR), continued
1.text: Self-service password reset (S S P R). The figure shows this: Self-service password reset flow: identify, verify with methods, reset. Exam tip: "Hybrid users reset passwords in the cloud and it must reach on-premises A D" equals enable password writeback.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An administrator wants users in the Sales department to join a group automatically. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A dynamic membership group. Dynamic groups use rules on user properties (Entra I D P one or higher).

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A license cannot be assigned to a new user. What is a likely missing setting? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The usage location. A usage location is required before assigning a license.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company wants all members of the Finance group to receive a Microsoft three sixty-five license automatically, including new members. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Group-based licensing. Group-based licensing assigns licenses to all members, including new ones.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A partner employee needs access to one application. What is the best way to give them an identity? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Invite them as a guest user. Guest users are the B to B collaboration identity for external people.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Hybrid users reset their passwords in the cloud, but the new password must work on-premises. What should be enabled? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Password writeback. Password writeback sends the new password to on-premises A D.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which S S P R setting decides how many proofs of identity a user must give? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The number of authentication methods required. The administrator sets the number of methods required.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is a guest user? Answer: An external person invited into your tenant. Question two. Which license level do dynamic groups need? Answer: Microsoft Entra I D P one or higher. Question three. What must a user have before a license is assigned? Answer: A usage location.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. For how long can a deleted user be restored? Answer: thirty days. Question five. What does S S P R stand for? Answer: Self-service password reset. Question six. What does password writeback do? Answer: Sends a cloud password reset to on-premises Active Directory.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Users: member versus guest; bulk create by C S V; deleted users recoverable thirty days. Groups: security versus Microsoft three sixty-five; assigned versus dynamic (P one plus ). Licenses: usage location needed; group-based licensing. External users: invite guests, control with collaboration settings. S S P R: scope, methods required, registration, password writeback.
